findings.title: Enum integer mappings for the spec-frozen values (0/1, plus 3 and 7) are UNPINNED — only 2 and 8 are pinned, indirectly, by the index backstop example
findings.detail: SPEC §1.2 freezes 'Values 0/1 untouched (live production rows)' and settles `trial_started: 7` / `trial_converted_to_paid: 8`. The enum block WAS edited by the diff, and the pre-diff comment mislabeled 0/1 in REVERSE (old comment: '0: assigned_free_plan / 1: assigned_free_plan_on_creation' vs the actual enum assigned_free_plan_on_creation: 0 / assigned_free_plan: 1) — a later 'fix code to match comment' agent swapping 0↔1 would relabel every live production row. Every spec asserts event_type by STRING name, so renumbering any value fails nothing. 2 and 8 are pinned only as a side effect of the RecordNotUnique backstop example (interactor spec:61): renumber either and the row falls outside the index predicate `event_type IN (2, 8)`, no conflict fires, and the count-eq-1 assertion fails. 0, 1, 3 (canceled_subscription — gains production rows at ship), and 7 have no pin of any kind.
findings.fix_shape: One falsifiable assertion of the full mapping, e.g. in the fanout or a model spec: `expect(SubscriptionEvent.event_types).to eq('assigned_free_plan_on_creation' => 0, 'assigned_free_plan' => 1, 'converted_to_paid' => 2, 'canceled_subscription' => 3, 'downgraded_to_free' => 4, 'upgraded_plan' => 5, 'downgraded_plan' => 6, 'trial_started' => 7, 'trial_converted_to_paid' => 8)`. Not a rule-26 tautology: it fails precisely on the renumbering threat (delete/renumber the enum and it fails); the stored integers ARE the production data contract.

findings.title: stripe_subscription_id argument SOURCE at both webhook writer sites is masked by same-value fixtures — swapping to organization.stripe_subscription_id passes every example
findings.detail: SPEC §5.2 mandates `stripe_subscription_id: object.subscription`; §5.3 mandates the branch-local `stripe_subscription_id` (= object.id). In every webhook example the event object's subscription id is constructed EQUAL to `organization.stripe_subscription_id` (invoice double `subscription: organization.stripe_subscription_id`, webhook spec:39; deleted double `id: organization.stripe_subscription_id`, spec:171), so replacing the spec-mandated event-sourced argument with the org column at either site is invisible to the whole suite. Production delta is real: a late invoice.paid or subscription.deleted for a subscription that is NOT the org's current one (resubscribe race, stale event) would write the row under the WRONG subscription id, corrupting the once-ever conversion uniqueness semantics the partial index enforces per stripe_subscription_id. Same masking sub-class as run 3's dedupe-masked duplicate example.
findings.fix_shape: One example per site with a DISTINCT event-object subscription id: invoice.paid — invoice `subscription: 'sub_evt_distinct'` while organization.stripe_subscription_id stays different, stub `Stripe::Subscription.retrieve.with('sub_evt_distinct')`, assert the row's stripe_subscription_id eq 'sub_evt_distinct'; subscription.deleted — deleted double `id: 'sub_evt_distinct'`, assert the row carries it (the sync_with_stripe equality guard then intentionally skips sync — do not assert sync in that example).

findings.title: 'Appended at the END of the branch' placement of both insertions is UNPINNED — reordering above existing lines passes every example
findings.detail: SPEC §5.2 mandates the invoice.paid insertion sit AFTER `organization_ai_credit_balance&.reset_ai_credits`; §5.3 mandates the deleted insertion sit AFTER the `EngagementReport::GeneratorJob` line. No example fails if either block is moved above earlier existing lines: the still-runs example (webhook spec:124) and the failure-isolation example (spec:135) assert effects, not order. Production delta (narrow, flagged for orchestrator judgment): if an existing line raises mid-branch (e.g. reset_ai_credits or the payment-method Stripe call), today NO ledger row is written and Stripe redelivery retries the whole branch; reordered, a conversion row is written for a delivery whose branch failed, and the once-ever uniqueness index then classifies the successful redelivery as a duplicate. Same structural-qualifier class as accepted r4-l1-a6-001 (`on: :create` scoping).
findings.fix_shape: invoice.paid: stub `organization.organization_ai_credit_balance.reset_ai_credits` to raise StandardError, deliver, assert not_to raise_error AND no SubscriptionEvent row (outer UNEXPECTED tier logs; insertion below the raise never runs — fails if the block is moved above). subscription.deleted: stub `EngagementReport::GeneratorJob` perform_later to raise, assert no row.
